solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Disdain, as against sweet talk

parts.note: con is the case against, as in pros and cons
to sweet-talk someone is to tempt or coax them

explanation.surface: Someone scorns flattery, seeing it as a thing to oppose.
explanation.definitionFit: Disdain and contempt are synonyms for scornful lack of respect.

clue.text: Minister I term mostly authoritative

parts.note: a canon is a cleric, a minister of a cathedral

indicators.note: mostly means all but the final letter of the word is kept

parts.note: to call something is to term or name it

explanation.surface: A clergyman says he uses a word in its most official sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Canonical texts are accepted as authentic and standard, carrying recognised authority.

clue.text: Journalist making various points, several inadequately

parts.note: the compass points north, east, west and south give N, E, W, S

indicators.note: inadequately means the word falls short, losing its last letter

parts.note: many means several

explanation.surface: A reporter makes several points, but not well enough.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsman is a reporter, someone who gathers and writes the news.

clue.text: Flowery English female opening gala

indicators.note: opening says the first pieces come at the start, before the festivity

parts.note: a fete is a gala or outdoor festivity

explanation.surface: An ornate Englishwoman opens a fete.
explanation.definitionFit: Effete describes affected, over-refined style, so flowery and precious in manner.

clue.text: Step into City University side by side

indicators.note: into says the step goes inside the city name

parts.note: Paris is the French capital city
pas is a step in ballet

explanation.surface: Someone walks into a city college.
explanation.definitionFit: Pari passu is Latin for 'with equal step', meaning on an equal footing, side by side.

clue.text: Person given time to go round shop

parts.note: bod is informal British slang for a person

indicators.note: going round here means turning the word for time back to front

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone is given a moment to pop round to the shops.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodega is a small grocery store or wine shop, in Spain or Spanish-speaking parts of the US.

clue.text: Armour as something that gives way?

definitions.meaning: a small round shield carried as protection
a thing that buckles, collapsing under pressure

explanation.definitionFit: A buckler is a small shield, and humorously it is a thing that buckles or gives way.

clue.text: Insect to keep going a long time? Crafty!

parts.words: to keep going a long time
parts.note: to drag on is to go on tediously for ages
fly is British slang for knowing, shrewd or crafty

explanation.surface: A cunning insect that seems to go on forever.
explanation.definitionFit: This long-bodied flying creature with two pairs of wings hunts near water.

clue.text: Leader of Girl Guides who could seem over-effusive?

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: ushers guide people to their seats

explanation.surface: A Girl Guide leader might come across as excessively gushing.
explanation.walkthrough: Girl Guides is the British girls' scouting group; here the words split apart.
explanation.definitionFit: People who gush talk with excessive enthusiasm, so they seem over-effusive.

clue.text: On return achieved victory right away

indicators.note: on return signals that the word for winning is read backwards

parts.note: to have achieved victory is to have won

explanation.surface: Coming back after a win, someone acts immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something now means doing it immediately, without delay.

clue.text: Super environment for new pupils?

definitions.meaning: super means excellent, of the highest quality
humorously, the ... a pupil joins at school

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful literal second reading: the very first classroom a child enters.
explanation.definitionFit: First-class means top quality, and read literally it is the earliest school class, where new pupils go.

clue.text: Label meant somehow to be attached to wild animal

indicators.note: somehow suggests the word meant can be rearranged in some way

parts.note: an ape is a wild animal, a primate

explanation.surface: A label is supposedly fixed onto a wild creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A name tape is a small fabric label sewn into clothing bearing the owner's name.

clue.text: John and Edward stripped

parts.note: john is slang for a lavatory, a loo
Ted is a familiar short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: Two men, John and Edward, took their clothes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' reads as a man's name beside Edward, but it is the slang word for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A place that has been plundered is stripped of its valuables.

clue.text: Some African sounds in headphones

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some music from Africa is played through headphones.
explanation.definitionFit: Cans is informal slang for headphones; the def phrase reads as 'what you find in headphones' with 'in' as part of it.

clue.text: Space by furnace to store fuel, by the sound of it?

indicators.note: by the sound of it means the words are heard spoken, not read

parts.note: to stow coal is to put fuel away

explanation.surface: A place near the boiler, apparently for keeping coal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stokehole is the space in front of a ship's furnace where stokers work.

clue.text: Father so furious with us shows propensity to lose temper

indicators.note: furious suggests wild agitation, so these letters are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: Dad is so angry with us that he shows a quick temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'furious' scrambles FATHER SO and US together.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a short fuse is an idiom for a tendency to get angry quickly, like a quickly burning detonator.

clue.text: Secretly occupying a space at the meal table?

definitions.meaning: done covertly, as an extra job or affair

definitions.text: occupying a space at the meal table?
definitions.meaning: like a side dish served next to the main course

explanation.definitionFit: Doing something covertly is an idiom; a side salad likewise sits beside the main plate.

clue.text: Height of joy ever only half grasped

indicators.note: grasped means held inside the word for joy

parts.note: elation is great joy

indicators.note: only half of a four-letter word means its first two letters

explanation.surface: The peak of happiness is only partly understood.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevation is the height of a place above sea level.

clue.text: The right expression for Napoleon?

parts.note: the French phrase for the exactly right word, as a Frenchman like Napoleon would say it

explanation.walkthrough: Napoleon stands for any French speaker: the answer is the French idiom for the perfect word, used in English too.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase translates as 'the exact word', the most fitting expression for something.

clue.text: US writer coming out, not the first person

indicators.note: not means the pronoun is taken away

parts.note: emersion is the act of emerging or coming out
I is the first-person pronoun

explanation.surface: An American author emerges, though not as the first one.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo Emerson was a nineteenth-century American essayist and poet.

clue.text: Environmentalist revealing evergreen shrub

definitions.meaning: Tony ... is a British campaigner, former head of Friends of the Earth
a conifer bearing berries used to flavour gin

explanation.definitionFit: Tony Juniper chairs Natural England; the plant is a coniferous bush whose berries flavour gin.

clue.text: University year's beginning with booze

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer, booze

explanation.surface: A university year starts with heavy drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Yale is an Ivy League university in Connecticut.

clue.text: A superior girl who achieved eminence in examination

parts.note: U stands for upper-class, as in the British U and non-U
Topsy is the girl in Uncle Tom's Cabin, read here as one who came out on top

explanation.surface: A snobbish girl rose to the top in a test.
explanation.walkthrough: U and non-U is the old British label for upper-class versus other usage.
explanation.definitionFit: An autopsy is a post-mortem examination of a body.

clue.text: Third man, not the first, to be seen outside the chapel

indicators.note: to be seen outside means the remaining letters go round the next word
not the first means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: Abel was the third man in Genesis, after Adam and Cain

explanation.surface: A man, ranked third rather than first, stands outside the chapel.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis only Adam and Cain precede him; 'not the first' leaves BEL, and 'to be seen outside' wraps that round the second 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bethel is a name for a nonconformist place of worship, especially a Methodist meeting house.

clue.text: Humble cleric entertaining your setter?

indicators.note: entertaining in the sense of holding as a guest, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a dean is a senior cleric in charge of a cathedral
the setter refers to themself, so me

explanation.surface: A modest clergyman plays host to the puzzle's compiler.
explanation.definitionFit: To humble someone is to lower their dignity, which is to demean them.

clue.text: Opening is possible with fastener loosened

indicators.note: loosened suggests the letters are freed from their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Undoing a clasp makes it possible to open something.
explanation.definitionFit: Fenestra is an anatomical term for a small window-like hole, such as in the inner ear.

clue.text: What helps Oxford to shine?

parts.note: an Oxford is a style of laced leather shoe, buffed with a waxy product

explanation.walkthrough: Oxford looks like the university or city; here it is the classic lace-up shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: This waxy paste is rubbed onto leather footwear to give it a gleam.

clue.text: Measure of acidity one found in Greek character

parts.note: pH is the scale measuring acidity
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An acidity reading is taken on a Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Phi is the twenty-first letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Wearing glad rags and ready to go?

definitions.meaning: glad rags are smart clothes, so dressed up in one's finery
a vehicle with its gears engaged is ready to move

explanation.definitionFit: Gear means clothing, so being dressed up fits; a car with a gear engaged is set to move off.

clue.text: This nonconformist (DV) may be newly saved, converted

indicators.note: converted suggests changing the letters into another form

parts.note: DV abbreviates Deo volente, God willing; set beside the answer its letters plus these make the phrase

explanation.surface: A dissenting believer, God willing, may be freshly saved and converted.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite: the answer plus DV, rearranged by 'converted', makes NEWLY SAVED.
explanation.definitionFit: Methodists following John Wesley's teaching were a nonconformist denomination outside the Church of England.
